items.stimulus: In 1924, geographer Elias Ward began mapping abandoned irrigation canals in California's Imperial Valley. He visited farms, consulted county records, and marked each canal on a hand-drawn chart. By 1928, Ward <u>had began</u> to compare the canals' construction dates with rainfall records. His findings suggested that several canals had been built during unusually wet years. Ward published a short report in 1931, but local officials initially paid little attention to it. In 1948, bureau archivists <u>found</u> Ward's maps in a storage room. They placed the surviving maps in a climate-controlled room and compared them with newer surveys. By 1970, researchers had <u><u>took</u></u> measurements from several canals that Ward had mapped. The resulting study helped historians understand how irrigation had shaped the valley's early farms.
items.explanation: After the auxiliary had, the irregular verb take must appear as its past participle, taken. The past perfect had taken also fits the By 1970 time frame.

per_choice.correct: After the auxiliary had, the irregular verb take must appear as its past participle, taken. The past perfect had taken also fits the By 1970 time frame.

items.stimulus: In 1934, surveyor Lena Okafor traveled to the high desert of New Mexico to document the region's ancient irrigation channels. Over the next three summers, she walked between isolated settlements and recorded the locations of stone-lined ditches. By the end of her first season, she had chose several channels for especially detailed study. At each site, she marked the channel's direction, measured its width, and photographed nearby terraces. The following year, Okafor returned to several sites to compare their condition with her earlier observations. When she revisited the northern valley, she <u>discovers</u> that heavy rains had damaged one of the oldest channels. She also interviewed local farmers, whose accounts helped her determine when the channels had last carried water. By the time the survey's maps were archived in 1938, Okafor had written a report that compared the channels' designs. Her records later helped historians understand how earlier communities had managed scarce water supplies. Today, copies of Okafor's maps are held by the New Mexico Historical Society.

When other researchers later examined the profiles, they confirmed that the ridge appeared in measurements from several parts of the ocean. Tharp continued refining her maps as new data arrived. By the time satellite measurements became available, her maps had gave researchers a useful framework for interpreting the ocean floor.

items.stimulus: In 1957, geologist Marie Tharp began compiling measurements of the Atlantic Ocean’s floor. At the time, much of the ocean remained unmapped, so Tharp worked with soundings gathered by research ships. She first converted those measurements into paper profiles that showed changes in depth. By the time the first set of charts was published, she <u>had drawed</u> a series of long, narrow diagrams. The profiles revealed a continuous ridge running down the middle of the Atlantic.
items.explanation: Draw is an irregular verb whose past participle is drawn, not drawed; after had, the past participle is required. The past perfect also correctly shows that the diagrams were completed before publication.

per_choice.correct: Draw is an irregular verb whose past participle is drawn, not drawed; after had, the past participle is required. The past perfect also correctly shows that the diagrams were completed before publication.
per_choice.trap: A writer may incorrectly regularize draw as drawed or use drew without noticing the auxiliary had.

items.trap: A writer may incorrectly regularize draw as drawed or use drew without noticing the auxiliary had.

items.stimulus: In 1957, geologist Marie Tharp began compiling measurements of the Atlantic Ocean’s floor. At the time, much of the ocean remained unmapped, so Tharp worked with soundings gathered by research ships. She first converted those measurements into paper profiles that showed changes in depth. By the time the first set of charts was published, she had drawed a series of long, narrow diagrams. The profiles revealed a continuous ridge running down the middle of the Atlantic. The pattern was significant because it supported the emerging theory of plate tectonics. Before the public saw the maps, Tharp’s colleague Bruce Heezen had present them at scientific meetings. When other researchers later examined the profiles, they confirmed that the ridge appeared in measurements from several parts of the ocean. Tharp continued refining her maps as new data arrived. By the time satellite measurements became available, her maps <u>had gave</u> researchers a useful framework for interpreting the ocean floor.
items.explanation: Give is irregular, and its past participle is given, so the correct form after had is had given. The past perfect appropriately describes what the maps had already done by the time satellite measurements became available.

per_choice.correct: Give is irregular, and its past participle is given, so the correct form after had is had given. The past perfect appropriately describes what the maps had already done by the time satellite measurements became available.
